notes: DIAGNOSIS — the store WRITE path is byte-correct; no UTF-8 truncation exists to fix. The suspected 'missing 4th site' (a note/acceptance buffer slicing a byte-array without backing off past continuation bytes) is not present. `src/managent/main.zig:1746 writeJsonString` emits every byte >= 0x20 verbatim and escapes only ", \, and control bytes (< 0x20), so a valid multi-byte note (— e2 80 94, → e2 86 92, é c3 a9) passes through unaltered. `serializeState` (:1295) and `writeStateLocked` (:1043) build into a growable `std.ArrayList(u8)` — there is no fixed-size note/acceptance buffer anywhere in the write path to slice (the only fixed buffers are `tmp_name_buf[256]` for the temp-file name and `normalizeRole`'s `buf[128]`, neither touches note text). The T399 write-site guard (:1056-1063) re-parses the serialized buffer with `std.json.parseFromSlice` and refuses the write on any invalid-JSON output, and that parser rejects invalid UTF-8 (verified: `"x \x80\x94 y"` → error.SyntaxError), so a mangled buffer could not reach disk through `writeStateLocked`. EVIDENCE the write path is clean: (1) add→claim→done→revert→status round-trips of notes/acceptances carrying —/→/é were byte-exact against the deployed `bin/managent` (built 13:34) AND a fresh `zig-out/bin/managent`; (2) a full 270-row copy of the live 333 KB store round-tripped with all note/verdict_note/impression/acceptance fields byte-identical; (3) an 80-process concurrent stress test (set/claim/status) kept the store valid JSON with the em-dash intact. ROOT CAUSE of the 2026-08-22 13:35:26Z corruption, best evidence: it is NOT reproducible from the committed write path. Timeline: `src/managent/main.zig` mtime 13:33:46 (T522 impression-gate work, uncommitted until 13:41 ee28e62), `bin/managent` deployed 13:34, corruption 13:35:26. The corrupting write therefore most likely came from a stale or mid-edit binary still on a fleet worker's PATH, not from the committed serializer — the T399 escaping + write-site guard have been in place since 2026-08-07 (7558775). DELIVERABLE (test-first per the standing rule; the defect could not be re-observed so the invariant is asserted rather than a bug re-introduced): `tools/regression-managent-store-write-utf8.sh` (new) — scratch store only, never the live kanban — asserts a note + bundle acceptance carrying —, →, é survive `add`/`claim`/`dispatch --note`/`set`/`done`(blocked)/`amend` byte-exact, and that `python3 -m json.tool` validates the store after every mutating verb, plus a `status --json` parse arm. Wired into `zig build test` (build.zig, `store_write_utf8_regression`). Standalone GREEN (all arms PASS). The full `zig build test` could not complete in-session because the pre-existing `tools/regression-dispatch.sh` fails (it live-dispatches worker tasks and waits 30 s for a worker to close them — unrelated to this change); the new regression itself is green. No live-store writes were made (scratch MANAGENT_STORE only). DIRECTIVE D021 (from deepseek-v4-pro/T568, acked 2026-08-22): census EVERY byte-slice in src/managent + one shared utf8Truncate + one class regression, and confirm the production write path is serialize→parse-back→atomic-rename (refuse unparseable store). CENSUS RESULT: 31 byte-slice sites enumerated across src/managent/main.zig; the ONLY free-text-truncating slices are the three T569 display sites (show note, assertion annotation, liveness command), already routed through the shared utf8Truncate; every other slice cuts at an ASCII delimiter (space, tab, newline, '-', '=', '-->', 'T<N>' prefix, ISO timestamp, path '/'), so the cut can never land inside a multi-byte sequence (continuation bytes are >= 0x80, never ASCII). The class is already single-helper + single-regression: the one regression here drives --/->/e through every mutating verb (add/claim/dispatch/set/done/amend). PRODUCTION WRITE PATH CONFIRMED: writeStateLocked serializes, re-parses the buffer via std.json.parseFromSlice and refuses the write on any unparseable output (T399 guard, src/managent/main.zig:1056-1063), then writes a tmp file + fsync + atomic rename (:1064-1082) — exactly serialize→parse-back→atomic-rename, with invalid-UTF-8 buffers refused (verified: parseFromSlice rejects 0x80 0x94 with error.SyntaxError).
